lines: Telling your AI "don't reveal secrets" is a hope with good phrasing.
By the time it reads that rule, it has already read the secret. Ask sideways, and it helpfully sums up the very file it was told to keep quiet.
The rule is a request. The context is a fact.
So put the door before the model. Every file says who it's for. A loader checks that against who's asking, and drops everything else before a single word reaches the model.
That's the whole fix: load context, with a role. And a file with no label? It counts as private. Hiding it by mistake costs one quick edit. Sharing it by mistake can't be undone.
Ask about a file it never got, and it just says: I don't have that. The model can't leak what it was never given.
facts: Every claim is from devweb.org/articles/deny-by-default-grounding (devweb content/articles/deny-by-default-grounding.mdx). I: 'It is a hope with good phrasing' (The wrong layer). II: 'By the time that instruction runs, the model has already read the confidential document'; 'A user asks the question sideways and the model, trying to be helpful, summarizes the very thing it was told to withhold.' III: 'The instruction is a request; the context is a fact.' IV: 'Filter the corpus at the loader, before the model sees anything'; 'Each document declares its audience in frontmatter; the loader checks that audience against the requester's role and either keeps the chunk or drops it'; 'before the model sees a single token'. V: load_context(corpus_root, role) (Filtering at the loader); 'a document with no audience marker defaults to internal, not shared'; over-restrict = 'fixes one frontmatter field'; over-share = 'There is no frontmatter edit that un-sends it.' (Deny by default, and the private floor). VI: the refusal 'I don't have that in the project context' (Refusal is the output); title and last line 'The model can't leak what it was never given.'
